question.text: Mr. Suresh Rao, CFO of Ananta Private Credit Fund (Cat II AIF), is drafting the tax section of the PPM for a fresh final close. Which combination of BASE disclosures is MOST aligned with the workbook's framework (Ch 16) and Finance Acts 2024/2025?

answer.text: (a) Fund is a company taxed at 25.168%; (b) TDS at 30% on all distributions; (c) GST at 28% on management fees.
(a) Cat III pass-through; (b) LTCG at 20% with indexation always; (c) STT at 0.5% on all trades.
(a) AIF is treated as a mutual fund under Section 115R; (b) distribution is subject to DDT.

(a) Fund is a 115UB 'Investment Fund' with pass-through on non-business income; (b) post FA 2025, Section 2(14) deems securities as capital assets; (c) TDS under Section 194LBB at 10% for residents and 20%/DTAA rate for NR dividend; (d) GST at 18% on management fees; (e) LTCG on unlisted > 24m at 12.5% without indexation; (f) cap of 15% surcharge on capital gains / dividend income of individuals.

explanation.text: The Logic: Option D bundles correct, current-law disclosures: Section 115UB perimeter; FA 2025 Section 2(14) amendment; 194LBB TDS rates; 18% GST on fees; post-23-07-2024 LTCG at 12.5% without indexation; FA 2022 15% surcharge cap on cap gains/dividend. All six items are workbook-sourced and current. The Trap: Option A recasts the fund as a company — most Cat II AIFs are trusts and use 115UB, not 115BAA. Option B invents Cat III pass-through and wrong STT. Option C applies MF/DDT regime to AIF — wrong framework. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests individual items at distributor level; XIX-C tests the manager's holistic PPM drafting. Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep a 'Tax Section' annex to the PPM reviewed by your tax counsel every 6 months. Post-Budget updates matter — FA 2024 changed LTCG rates, FA 2025 changed 2(14). A stale PPM tax section invites SEBI-Regulation-10(1)(g) material-disclosure issues on subsequent closes.
